items.proof_plan: Pair the relative groups of skeletal pairs by the external product, the collapse to the (p,r) block of the product filtration quotient, and pullback along the cellular diagonal, giving a typed bilinear mu_1: E_1^{p,q} x E_1^{r,s} -> E_1^{p+r,q+s} together with the corresponding pairing of the relative D-terms; naturality of the external product makes the restriction, connecting and pair maps multiplicative. The two relative connecting-map Leibniz identities give d_1 mu_1(x,y) = mu_1(d_1x,y) + (-1)^{p+q} mu_1(x,d_1y) for d_1 = jk, so mu_1 carries cycles to cycles and sends B x Z + Z x B to boundaries and descends to a pairing mu_2 on E_2 = H(E_1,d_1). Forgetting support gives F^p F^q contained in F^{p+q}, and finite convergence identifies the stable product with the associated-graded product. Only the ring products from E_2 on, their derivations and the ring isomorphism E_{r+1} = H(E_r,d_r) are taken from the standard multiplicative structure of a pairing of filtering towers; step 7.2 records an explicit six-segment cellular diagonal of the interval whose first-page pairing is not associative, so no E_1 ring is asserted.

items.statement: Let h be a reduced generalized cohomology theory with a coherent external product (unital, associative, graded-commutative, compatible with suspension, with the two relative connecting-map Leibniz identities). For a finite CW complex with skeleta X^p and a cellular approximation of the diagonal: the relative products of skeletal pairs, the collapse to the (p,r) block and the diagonal give a typed bilinear pairing mu_1: E_1^{p,q} x E_1^{r,s} -> E_1^{p+r,q+s} with E_1^{p,q}=h^{p+q}(X^p,X^{p-1}), and the same construction pairs h^m(X,X^{p-1}) with h^n(X,X^{r-1}) into h^{m+n}(X,X^{p+r-1}); mu_1 is natural for morphisms of theories and for cellular maps whose chosen filtered diagonals commute strictly, but no naturality is claimed for independently chosen diagonals, and it carries no associativity, graded commutativity or unitality in general. d_1 = jk satisfies the Leibniz rule with respect to mu_1, and mu_1 descends to a pairing mu_2 on E_2 = H(E_1,d_1); from E_2 on the products make every page a natural unital associative graded-commutative bigraded ring on which d_r is a derivation, with E_{r+1} = H(E_r,d_r) as bigraded rings and mu_2 the graded cup product under E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X;h^q(*)), so the product is independent of the diagonal from the second page on. The filtration is multiplicative, F^p F^q contained in F^{p+q}, and E_infinity = gr_F h^*(X) as graded rings.

items.proof_plan: Apply the pairing lemma. It supplies the typed first-page pairing, its Leibniz rule for d_1, the descent to E_2, the ring products and derivations from E_2 on, the ring isomorphism E_{r+1} = H(E_r,d_r), the identification of the E_2 product with the graded cup product and hence independence from the chosen diagonal, filtration multiplicativity and the stable associated-graded product. The theorem therefore asserts multiplicativity from the second page on and records that the first page carries only the pairing and its Leibniz rule, since the lemma's explicit six-segment diagonal of the interval makes the first-page pairing non-associative.

items.statement: If h has a specified unital, associative, graded-commutative coherent external product compatible with suspension and satisfying the two relative cofiber-boundary Leibniz identities, then for a finite CW complex and a cellular approximation of the diagonal the cohomological AHSS is multiplicative from its second page on: the relative products and the diagonal pair the skeletal exact couple with itself, that pairing satisfies the Leibniz rule for d_1 and descends to E_2; for every r ≥ 2 the page E_r is a unital associative graded-commutative bigraded ring on which d_r is a derivation with E_{r+1} = H(E_r,d_r) as bigraded rings; the E_2 product is the graded cup product under E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X;h^q(*)), hence independent of the diagonal; the filtration is multiplicative and E_infinity = gr_F h^*(X) as graded rings. The first page carries the pairing and its Leibniz rule but is not a ring in general. A ring prespectrum is only an example of the hypotheses.

items.proof_plan: The displayed bidegree sends an even coefficient row under d₂ to an odd coefficient group, which is zero, so d₂=0 and E₃=E₂. First handle p=0, where the positive-degree Postnikov argument does not apply. A finite CW complex has finitely many path components. On each component X_a, every x∈H^0(X_a;Z) is the pullback of an integer along X_a→*. AHSS naturality gives d₃(x) as the pullback of d₃ on the point, whose H^3 target is zero; restriction to all components therefore gives d₃(x)=0. Instability also gives Sq²ρ₂(x)=0, so β_ZSq²ρ₂(x)=0. For p≥1, Bott-translate the coefficient row to q≤0. The preceding representability/comparison lemma identifies the local K-AHSS d₃ with the first representing-space ku Postnikov obstruction, including the p=1 suspension reduction and the finite-pair case. The connective-k-invariant lemma identifies that obstruction with β_ZSq²ρ₂. Transport back through the fixed natural Bott isomorphisms; naturality for theory morphisms makes these isomorphisms maps of skeletal exact couples. A possible global sign from the long-exact-sequence convention is immaterial because the operation has order two.

items.title: Integral complex projective bundle theorem

items.proof_plan: Adopt the unique coefficients and specialize the rank-one relation P(L)=B.
items.statement: Assume AC. Define c_i(E)=a_i in x^n-c_1x^{n-1}+⋯+(-1)^nc_n=0, with c_0=1 and c_i=0 above rank; for a line c_1=e(L_R).
items.title: Chern classes from the projective-bundle relation

items.proof_plan: Iterate the CW-type projective construction proved in the projective-bundle theorem. Orthogonal projections give locally trivial complements; partitions of unity give their numerability. Compact-fiber total-space preservation licenses each next stage. There are no stages when n=1.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §3, splitting principle by iterated projectivization, printed pp. 208–210
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. Iterated projectivization and Hermitian complements give q:Fl(E)→B with q^*E=L_1⊕⋯⊕L_n; t_i=c_1(L_i) are the Chern roots.
items.title: Complex flag bundle and Chern roots

items.proof_plan: Each original CW-base flag tower has coefficient-of-one injective projective maps. For multiple bundles pull their original towers back successively; projectivization and numeration commute with pullback and the CW-type projective theorem applies at each stage. Pull the original splittings back. Omit zero ranks and use the identity for an empty family.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §3, splitting principle and splitting lemma, printed pp. 208–210
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. The flag projection splits q^*E into lines and has injective q^*:H^*(B;R)→H^*(Fl(E);R) for R=Z and for every field F_p. Finitely many bundles have a common such splitting space with coefficientwise injective pullback.
items.title: Complex splitting principle with integral injective pullback

items.proof_plan: Use the projective-bundle pullback square and coefficient uniqueness for naturality; on a common splitting space multiply line factors and descend by injectivity.
items.statement: Assume AC. Chern classes are pullback natural, c_1(L)=e(L_R), and c(E⊕F)=c(E)c(F), including rank-zero and stabilization conventions.
items.title: Naturality, normalization, and Whitney sum for Chern classes

items.proof_plan: Prove the flag total path-connected through its projective tower and choose an actual path-connected CW model h:C->Fl(E). Evaluate d and c only on C, where the pulled-back bundle splits into numerable lines. Naturality along p=q h and injectivity of p*=h* q* descend the equality; treat rank zero separately.

references.locator: Chapter 23 §7, Chern-class axioms and uniqueness, printed pp. 197–200
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. Natural assignments on isomorphism classes of numerable complex bundles over nonempty path-connected CW complexes, normalized by degree zero one, rank cutoff, and d_1(L)=e(L_R), and satisfying Whitney multiplication, are uniquely the Chern classes.
items.title: Uniqueness of Chern classes from the splitting principle

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from bundle classification and the cohomological Kunneth theorem.
items.proof_plan: Identify orthogonal flags with the torus quotient by explicit frame charts. Prove the finite product circle model is classifying using coordinate quotients and fiber products. The ordered-line map is a homotopy equivalence by the natural fibration sequence and Whitehead after a CW model. Compute roots by Euler naturality and Kunneth, then use permutation homeomorphisms over the Grassmannian.

references.locator: Lectures 34–35, universal flag bundle, maximal torus and splitting principle, printed pp.123–132
references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.statement: For n>=1 under AC, the universal complex flag bundle is the quotient model BT^n over BU(n), and the explicit ordered-line map to the finite product of CP-infinity spaces is a homotopy equivalence identifying roots with tautological Euler generators. Permutations fix the image of flag pullback.
items.title: The universal complex flag bundle is BT-n

items.proof_plan: Apply integral splitting to the universal bundle, so q^* is injective. The flag-space lemma identifies the target as Z[t_1,…,t_n] and puts the image inside its symmetric invariants. Whitney multiplication after splitting sends q^*c_i to the ith elementary symmetric polynomial e_i. Hence the image contains Z[e_1,…,e_n], while the fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials says this is the entire invariant ring. Therefore q^* identifies H^*(BU(n);Z) with Z[e_1,…,e_n], proving both generation and algebraic independence without a Gysin or finite-index shortcut. Apply Whitney on the actual product CW model and descend by homotopy-invariant cohomology, using Euler naturality for line roots on the CW-type flag model.
items.statement: For n>=1 under AC, H^*(BU(n);Z)=Z[c_1,...,c_n] for the associated tautological vector bundle; flag pullback sends c_i to e_i in the coordinate roots.
items.title: Integral cohomology of BU(n)

items.proof_plan: Identify BU(1)=CP∞ with K(Z,2), and use bundle classification plus representability to obtain the natural bijection. The universal c1 is the integral generator by the projective-bundle normalization. On CP∞×CP∞, Kunneth makes H² free on the two coordinate generators; the tensor product of universal lines restricts to the universal line on either axis, so naturality forces its c1 to be their sum. Pullback proves that tensor product corresponds to addition for every allowed base. Use the exact pointed-set tail only to show pi_1=0 for the connected circle fiber. HEP at the vertex and cohomology representability explicitly identify based and free classes. Transport the group isomorphism to CW-type bases by the natural classification/cohomology square.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a path-connected CW complex with vertex basepoint, and more generally a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CGWH space of CW type, c_1 gives a natural group isomorphism from numerable line-bundle classes under tensor product to H^2(-;Z).
items.title: The first Chern class classifies complex line bundles

items.proof_plan: Use the Picard group isomorphism, L⊗L*=1, and the metric-induced complex-linear isomorphism from the conjugate line to L*.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §4, first-Chern tensor formula, printed pp. 211–212
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. On a path-connected CW base with vertex, or a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CGWH base of CW type, numerable complex lines satisfy c_1(L tensor M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M), c_1(L*)=-c_1(L), c_1(conjugate L)=-c_1(L).
items.title: First Chern class of tensor, dual, and conjugate lines

items.proof_plan: After splitting, both are the product of line Euler classes; descend by integral injectivity and retain the complex orientation.
items.statement: Assume AC. For complex rank-n E with its complex orientation, c_n(E)=e(E_R).
items.title: Top Chern class equals Euler class of the underlying real bundle

items.proof_plan: Pull the flag splitting to an actual CW model, retain mod-two injectivity, multiply line identities there, and use both characteristic-class naturalities and coefficient naturality to descend.
items.statement: Assume AC. For complex E, w_{2i+1}(E_R)=0 and w_{2i}(E_R)=ρ_2c_i(E).
items.title: Mod-two reduction of Chern classes

items.proof_plan: Glue complexification using the real transitions and use coordinate conjugation for its canonical complex-linear comparison. For a positive-rank V pull the flag splitting to a CW model; Whitney and the line conjugation formula negate each root. Injectivity of the composite pullback descends the sign formula. Treat rank zero directly by conventions.
items.statement: Assume AC. For real E its complexification is canonically complex-linearly isomorphic to its conjugate; for every complex V, conjugation sends c_i(V) to (−1)^ic_i(V).
items.title: Complexification is conjugation invariant

items.proof_plan: Combine E_C≅its conjugate with the odd sign in the conjugation formula.
items.statement: Assume AC. For real E, 2c_{2j+1}(E_C)=0; integral vanishing is not claimed.
items.title: Odd Chern classes of a complexified real bundle are two-torsion

items.proof_plan: Record the complexification, sign, degree, rank cutoff and orientation independence.
items.statement: Assume AC. For real rank-n E define p_i(E)=(−1)^ic_{2i}(E_C)∈H^{4i}(B;Z), with p_0=1 and p_i=0 for 2i>n; no orientation is required.
items.title: Pontryagin classes by complexification

items.proof_plan: Check complexification/pullback and sum comparisons by transition matrices. Give the real-linear isomorphism (E_C)_R to E plus E and its inverse. Apply the exact mod-two Chern supplier, use graded commutativity in characteristic two to cancel cross terms, and check both rank cutoffs.
items.statement: Assume AC. For numerable real bundles over nonempty path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CW bases, Pontryagin classes are natural for continuous maps between those bases, stable, and satisfy rho_2 p_i=w_{2i}^2.
items.title: Naturality, stability, and mod-two reduction of Pontryagin classes

items.proof_plan: Expand the Chern Whitney product, retain even-even terms, and observe every discrepancy contains odd complexification Chern classes killed after inverting two.
items.statement: Assume AC. Over Z[1/2], or any coefficient ring with 2 invertible, p(E⊕F)=p(E)p(F); integrally the omitted odd-Chern cross terms can obstruct this formula.
items.title: Pontryagin Whitney product away from two

items.proof_plan: Use the explicit real isomorphism from clause 3 of the complex-orientation lemma. Count n(2n-1) interchanges from interleaved to product frame, so the sign is (-1)^n. Top Chern equals complex-oriented Euler and Whitney Euler multiplication then cancel the defining Pontryagin sign. Handle canonical rank zero separately.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a numerable oriented real rank-2n bundle over a nonempty path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CW base, p_n=e^2 integrally. Rank zero has its canonical unit orientation; orientation reversal is asserted only for n>0.
items.title: Top Pontryagin class is the square of the Euler class

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; numerations, compact-fiber CW-type comparison and Euler-class suppliers.
items.proof_plan: Use graph charts and compact-fiber admissibility. Construct r by the oriented perpendicular complement and inverse s(W)=(R e_1 plus P W,e_1), P the even-coordinate embedding. Descend the equivariant Gram-normalized parity homotopy and rotate Pv to e_1 to prove both inverse homotopies. Split by av+w with the trivial line first; apply Euler naturality and the nonzero section. BSO(1) is contractible, not literally a point.

references.locator: Lectures 35–36, universal oriented sphere bundles and BSO induction, printed pp.130–137
references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II
Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Lemma 1.15 pp.28–29; parity argument p.30; Proposition 1.19 p.36 (paracompact numerations for compact exhaustions); oriented complement p.95.

items.statement: For n>=2 the actual sphere bundle S_n of the universal oriented n-plane is a Hurewicz fibration over BSO(n), and complement r:S_n->BSO(n-1) is a homotopy equivalence. With v-first complement orientation the ordered splitting is epsilon^1 plus r*gamma_(n-1), and p*e=0.
items.title: The universal oriented sphere-bundle total space has the homotopy type of BSO(n-1)

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC chooses the simplex lifts used to define transfer simultaneously.
items.proof_plan: Prove freeness by uniqueness of lifts and transitivity by the regular-cover definition, hence |G|=d for nonempty covers. Prove simplex lifting and face-restriction bijections with the lifting criterion. Form the full lift-sum chain map, dualize to transfer, verify T p*=d and p*T=sum g*, divide by d and use cup naturality. Treat the empty case separately.

references.locator: §3.G, transfer homomorphisms for finite-sheeted coverings, printed pp.321–326
references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite d-sheeted regular CW covering with d>=1, regular meaning path-connected total space and fiber-transitive deck group, rational pullback is injective with image precisely the deck-invariant graded subalgebra; the empty case gives zero groups.
items.title: Rational transfer identifies a finite regular cover with deck invariants

items.proof_plan: Induct on n from BSO(1) contractible, assuming only P(n-1). Even n: sphere restriction surjects onto the preceding polynomial ring; Gysin makes multiplication by e injective, giving generation by degree induction and independence by finite E-degree induction. Odd n: Euler is rationally zero; inject into the preceding even ring and compare finite dimensions with its subring generated by p_i and e^2. Use the actual sphere total and its homotopy equivalence via j=p s, never a literal equality. Apply rational transfer to the connected orientation double cover, fixing p_i and negating positive even-rank e.

references.title: Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Proposition 1.19, printed p.36 (complete proof); paragraph preceding Theorem 3.16, printed p.94; rational/away-from-two Gysin induction and transfer, printed pp.95–96.

items.statement: Assume AC. For m≥1, H^*(BO(2m);Q)=H^*(BO(2m+1);Q)=Q[p_1,…,p_m], H^*(BSO(2m+1);Q)=Q[p_1,…,p_m], and H^*(BSO(2m);Q)=Q[p_1,…,p_{m-1},e], with p_m=e². BO(0) and BSO(0) are points; BSO(1) is the contractible stable unit sphere. All have rational cohomology Q.
items.title: Rational cohomology of BO and BSO by Pontryagin and Euler classes

items.proof_plan: The cellular cochain complex of a finite CW complex is concentrated in degrees at most the dimension, and cellular cochains compute singular cohomology with the trivial local system.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a CW pair (X,A) with X finite of dimension d and any coefficient ring R, H^n(X,A;R)=0 for n>d; in particular H^n(X;R)=0 above the dimension.
items.title: Cohomology of a finite CW complex vanishes above its dimension

items.proof_plan: Symmetric-polynomial theory descends the root expression uniquely; finite dimension makes each evaluated total degree finite.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a complex vector bundle E over a finite CW complex X, define ch(E)=Σexp(t_i) in the direct sum H^{even}(X;Q); each homogeneous term is the corresponding rational Newton polynomial in c_1,…,c_n, and finite dimension leaves only finitely many nonzero evaluated terms.
items.title: Chern character of a complex vector bundle
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; Chern, Euler, numerable-fibration, universal coefficient and Leray–Hirsch suppliers.

items.proof_plan: On a common splitting space, sums concatenate roots and tensors replace them by t_i+u_j; exponential identities prove both formulas, then injectivity and Grothendieck universality finish. Naturality and the internal product on X×Y then give the external formula ch(a external-product b)=ch(a) external-product ch(b) by writing the external product as the product of the two projection pullbacks.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §4, Chern-character construction and ring-homomorphism lemma, printed pp. 211–212
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite CW complex X, the Chern character is natural, additive on sums and multiplicative on tensors, hence extends uniquely through Grothendieck completion to a unital ring map ch:K^0(X)→H^{even}(X;Q).
items.title: Chern character is a natural ring homomorphism on K-zero

items.proof_plan: Construct the reduced and odd maps before the graded map; iterate Bott and check independence of the even shift using the Bott normalization. For products, use the external-product formula in degree zero. Represent each odd class by a reduced degree-zero class on a suspension; the product diagram uses ΣX_+ smash ΣY_+ isomorphic to Σ²(X×Y)_+, and desuspension by the Bott class. The normalization ch(beta)=the rational S² suspension generator makes this diagram commute. The sphere twist supplies the same Koszul sign in K-theory and cohomology, so even-even, even-odd, and odd-odd external products are all preserved; diagonal pullback gives the internal Z/2-graded product.
items.statement: Assume AC. Restrict the degree-zero Chern character to the kernel of basepoint restriction, retaining ranks on other components. Define degree -1 by suspension, and all integer degrees by the fixed Bott maps, normalized by ch(beta)=c1(gamma). Naturality and products use the coherent suspension products.
items.title: Graded Chern character by suspension and Bott periodicity

items.proof_plan: Use the cofiber of A+ to X+ for actual K and ordinary cohomology, collar excision and X+ for empty A. Normalize pair boundaries as -q*s to match the ordinary cochain boundary; apply based character naturality/suspension. Filtration is preserved by naturality of restriction into HP.
items.statement: Assume AC. For finite CW pairs, the graded character gives maps on relative groups commuting with connecting maps and sends the K-theory skeletal filtration F^p into the ordinary-cohomology filtration F^p.
items.title: The graded Chern character respects relative maps and skeletal filtrations
items.axiom_audit: AC inherited from actual K-theory and graded character; no arbitrary reduced/pair correspondence is used.

items.proof_plan: Construct actual pair exact couples; prove rational tensor exactness by fractions and identify rationalized derived pages. The relative graded character induces a couple morphism; first-page finite-cell coefficient maps are isomorphisms by Bott normalization, hence so are second-page maps. Check stable filtration compatibility by representative maps.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite CW complex, after tensoring with Q the filtered character induces an AHSS morphism whose E2 coefficient map is K^q(*)⊗Q≅Q for even q and zero-to-zero for odd q.
items.title: Chern character induces the rational isomorphism on AHSS E-two

items.proof_plan: E2 comparison gives E∞ comparison. Identify it with gr(ch), then lift through the finite filtration by short exact sequences and the five lemma; rational collapse alone is not used to identify filtered groups. The preceding graded construction already proves multiplicativity in all parity combinations, so the additive bijections in the two parity classes together are a bijective Z/2-graded ring homomorphism.

references.locator: Chapter 24 §4, Chern character and statement of the finite-CW rational isomorphism, printed pp. 211–212
references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.statement: Assume AC. For every finite CW complex X and every integer j, ch⊗Q:K^j(X)⊗Q→⊕_kH^{j+2k}(X;Q) is a natural filtered additive isomorphism. Taken over both parity classes, these maps form an isomorphism of Z/2-graded rings.
items.title: Rational Chern character isomorphism for finite CW complexes

title: Chern and Pontryagin Classes by Splitting and Complexification

items.proof_plan: Duality and tautological Euler generation; compute the hyperplane Euler number +1 using the coordinate-functional section and its normalized Thom pullback at its unique zero.
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥1, tautological γ over CP^n and the positive generator x=c_1(γ^*) satisfy c_1(γ)=−x and c(γ^*)=1+x.
items.title: Chern class of tautological and hyperplane lines on complex projective space

items.proof_plan: Iterate line normalization and the Whitney product, then take homogeneous components.
items.statement: Assume AC. On (CP∞)^n, for E=⊕L_i and x_i=c_1(L_i), c(E)=∏(1+x_i) and c_k is the kth elementary symmetric polynomial.
items.title: Chern classes of a sum of universal complex lines

items.proof_plan: The circle fundamental-group theorem and the power-map degree calculation identify the clutching map z↦z^d with d times the Hopf clutching generator. The published Hopf-line calculation fixes the d=1 bundle and orientation. The c1 classification is a group isomorphism, so tensor/clutching addition sends the class to d·u, including negative d and d=0.
items.statement: Assume AC. For d∈Z and the positive generator u∈H²(S²;Z) fixed by the Hopf orientation, the line over S² clutched by z↦z^d has c_1=d·u; clutching degree and first Chern number give the same Z-classification.
items.title: Complex line bundles over the two-sphere by clutching degree

items.proof_plan: Specialize the top-Chern/Euler and mod-two comparison theorems to rank one with complex orientation.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a complex line L, e(L_R)=c_1(L), w_1(L_R)=0, and w_2(L_R)=ρ_2c_1(L).
items.title: Realification of a complex line compares c-one, w-two, and Euler

items.proof_plan: Use total class one for a trivial summand, the stability formulas, and the defining rank cutoffs.
items.statement: Assume AC. Over a nonempty path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CW base, for trivial ε^r one has c(E⊕ε^r)=c(E) and p(F⊕ε^r)=p(F); c_i vanishes above complex rank and p_i when 2i exceeds real rank.
items.title: Stability and rank cutoff under adding a trivial summand

items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the characteristic-class and projective-space suppliers.
items.proof_plan: For the universal line the rank-one real projective-bundle definition identifies w_1(λ) with the tautological class u. The underlying real bundle of λ_C is canonically λ⊕λ via v⊗(a+ib)↦(av,bv). Mod-two Chern reduction and Whitney multiplication therefore give ρ_2(a)=w_2(λ⊕λ)=u². The polynomial ring H^*(RP^∞;F_2)=F_2[u] makes u^{2k} nonzero, so ρ_2(a^k)=u^{2k}≠0. The odd-Chern complexification theorem gives 2a=0, hence 2a^k=0; nonzero reduction shows every a^k is a nonzero class of exact order two.

references.locator: Lecture 36, complexification and the two-torsion obstruction to integral Pontryagin multiplication, printed pp.134–137
references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.statement: Assume AC. Let λ be the universal real line on RP^∞, u=w_1(λ), and a=c_1(λ_C). Then 2a=0, ρ_2(a)=u², and for every k≥1 the class a^k is nonzero of exact order two with ρ_2(a^k)=u^{2k}.
items.title: Integral powers of the complexified universal real line

items.proof_plan: The preceding lemma proves a²≠0 with no appeal to an additive UCT calculation. Since E_C=λ_C⊕λ_C, Whitney multiplication gives c_2(E_C)=a² and therefore p_1(E)=-a²≠0. Every positive p_i(λ) vanishes by the real-rank cutoff, so p(λ)p(λ)=1.
items.statement: Assume AC. For the universal real line λ over RP∞ and E=λ⊕λ, p_1(E)=−a²≠0 for a=c_1(λ_C) of order two, while p(λ)p(λ)=1 by rank cutoff.
items.title: Integral total Pontryagin multiplicativity cannot ignore two-torsion
